title: Existence of the unit-normalized evaluation comparison
statement: theorem inverseEvaluation_exists {X Y : Scheme.{t}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (n : ℕ) : ∃ ξ : inverse l E f ⋙ coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E X n ≅ coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E Y n ⋙ integralOperationsLevelPullback l E f n, ∀ M : coefficientSequenceModules l E Y, (coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E Y n).map ((Adjunction.ofIsRightAdjoint (direct l E f)).unit.app M) ≫ (eqToIso (directEvaluation_eq l E f n)).hom.app ((inverse l E f).obj M) ≫ (Scheme.coefficientProEtaleModuleDirectImage.{t, u} f (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{t + 1} (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1))))).map (ξ.hom.app M) = (Scheme.coefficientProEtaleModuleAdjunction.{t, u} f (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{t + 1} (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1))))).unit.app ((coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E Y n).obj M)

proof.text: Apply the existing sequence-module inverse-image evaluation theorem to the actual base-change functor, sequence coefficient ring map, its finite ring map, the chosen system adjunction and the canonical finite adjunction. The right-adjoint evaluation isomorphism is eqToIso of directEvaluation_eq, which is a natural isomorphism. The theorem makes its inverse mate invertible. Invert that mate to obtain the required evaluation isomorphism. The identity unit_mateEquiv_symm, postcomposed with the image of the inverse mate, gives exactly the required unit normalization after functorial inverse cancellation.
